newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia said facing numerous economic problems.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia said facing numerous economic problems.

text.p: Yugoslavia faced numerous economic problems, including an apparatchik mentality which threatened foreign ties, a prominent business official said.
Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce president Mihajlo Milojevic saw apparatchik mentality as one of the key threats to an economy struggling to restore ties with the world and attract foreign investors.

"Apparatchik mentality and behaviour are threats we must run away from. Parts of our administration lack understanding and readiness for technical and production cooperation with foreigners," Milojevic said.
Due to such behaviour foreign partners who invested capital and technology enjoyed no practical advantages, he added.
The country's GDP is planned to grow 13 percent in 1997, industrial output 13.9 percent and exports almost 47 percent.
But January-June industrial output rose 7.6 percent year-on-year while exports grew 28.5 percent, with the trade gap exceeding $1 billion, The chamber said in a half-year review.
Reasons for the failure to meet growth targets in the first half of 1997 included lack of liquidity in the economy, lack of financial discipline, oversized public spending and uncontrolled imports.
"Constant export growth and imroved performance is imperative," Milojevic said.

"Economic problems are numerous and we must not be satisfied with five, six or seven percent growth because we fell too low during the embargo. Those rates must be higher and we must quickly return to 1989/90 levels," he said.
